extracted.intended_audience: webcomic creators, humorists, and fans studying xkcd-style humor
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing or evaluating short webcomics in the style of xkcd: minimal stick-figure visuals, science/tech/mathematics framing, layered jokes (including hover/alt-text), and reductio ad absurdum premises that reward both expertise and accessible feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core appeal: topical focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on science, mathematics, technology, and general geekiness with light, quirky humor and occasional profound philosophizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target subject matter toward STEM/technical domains and 'geek' culture; tone should be lightly quirky and occasionally philosophical rather than purely topical or celebrity-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual + Emotional
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor both intellectually stimulating and emotionally resonant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on slapstick or purely topical gags; instead combine cognitive surprises (logic, math, technical framing) with emotionally relatable human experience. Delve into fundamental principles of science, logic, or behavior so the joke lands on both levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise language for absurdity
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses scientific language to dissect everyday absurdities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame everyday scenarios in mathematical/programming terms (unit-conversion jokes, edge cases, hypothetical extremes). Precision in wording and formalism is used to expose absurd conclusions or contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stick-figure minimalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Stick figures = readers project; specific look would distract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep visuals extremely simple so the art doesn't compete with the idea; clean visuals foreground the joke and allow wide reader projection onto characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alt text reward / layered punch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alt-text (or analogous layered elements) to provide a secondary punchline or meta-commentary. Structure the joke so engagement (e.g., hovering) is rewarded with an extra layer without making it required to get the main gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reductio ad absurdum / 'What If?'
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a premise to its logical extreme; 'What If?' answers serious-seeming questions absurdly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from a plausible-seeming technical or conceptual premise and push it to an extreme outcome using rigorous-seeming reasoning; the dissonance between formality and absurd conclusion creates the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring engines / motifs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurring comedic engines used by the comic include misuse of statistics, standards proliferation, map projections, programming jokes, and romance via spreadsheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage recognizable recurring patterns (e.g., 'Correlation doesn't imply causation, but…', 'Now there are 15 standards', map-projection obsessions, compile-error style panels, treating romance as data) so readers familiar with the genre get additional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a precise (scientific/logical) framing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the joke is anchored by a formal, scientific, or logical setup—precision in framing is a hallmark of the style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the precision intersect everyday human experience?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the precision intersect everyday human experience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the technical framing connects to relatable human situations or feelings; the tension between formalism and everyday life is key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the visual minimal, foregrounding the joke?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the visual minimal, foregrounding the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the artwork is intentionally simple so that readers focus on the idea rather than detailed illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a layered punch (alt text, secondary)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a layered punch (alt text, secondary)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the comic contains multiple layers of payoff (e.g., main panel gag plus alt-text joke) that reward different levels of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it reward expertise without excluding novices?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it reward expertise without excluding novices?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic should contain references or precision that experts appreciate, but the core joke must remain accessible to readers without specialist knowledge; avoid gating the entire joke behind niche knowledge.
